answers:
You do not need to create a new middleware. In laravel 11, you can go to bootstrap/app.php and add URIs in except array.
$middleware->validateCsrfTokens(except: [
    'stripe/*',
    'http://example.com/foo/bar',
    'http://example.com/foo/*',
]);

Further detail can be found here.

In Laravel 11, configure CSRF exclusions directly in `bootstrap/app.php`; a custom `VerifyCsrfToken` subclass is unnecessary for this purpose. Page 1 documents `validateCsrfTokens(except: [...])`.

Remove your CSRF `web(replace: [...])` block and add this inside your existing `withMiddleware` callback:

```php
$middleware->validateCsrfTokens(
    except: ['profile/contact']
);
```

Keep your other middleware configuration as needed.

According to page 1, middleware that previously lived in new applications—including CSRF validation—has moved into the framework itself. This explains why you do not need to explicitly add CSRF middleware to your application.

The `bootstrap/app.php` file has been revitalized as a code-first application configuration file. From this file, you may now customize your application's routing, middleware, service providers, exception handling, and more. This file unifies a variety of high-level application behavior settings that were previously scattered throughout your application's file structure:

```php
return Application::configure(basePath: dirname(__DIR__))
    ->withRouting(
These middleware performed a variety of tasks such as authenticating requests, trimming input strings, and validating CSRF tokens.

In Laravel 11, these middleware have been moved into the framework itself, so that they do not add bulk to your application's structure. New methods for customizing the behavior of these middleware have been added to the framework and may be invoked from your application's `bootstrap/app.php` file:

```

Since all middleware can be easily customized via your application's `bootstrap/app.php`, the need for a separate HTTP "kernel" class has been eliminated.
